title: NL coast: easy hour, firm sand
terrain: firm wet sand at the waterline, flat, no dunes today
coachNotes: Last day of the flat block, fly home tonight. Easy hour, nothing to prove. NO DUNES TODAY: Saturday took the vertical and the calves will know it, and a second sand-climbing day 48h apart two weeks out is how a new surface turns into an Achilles problem. Flat firm sand only. BEACH CAMBER: turn around every 10-15 minutes so the same leg is not on the low side for an hour, or run the flattest band above the high tide line. A canted surface is a documented ITBS provoker and it is the one avoidable risk on this beach. If the calves are sore from Saturday, run the road instead and lose nothing. GUT TRAINING: 60 g/h from minute 30, on this run too, easy or not. Transporter capacity adapts over roughly two weeks of repeated exposure, so every run over an hour between now and 5 September is part of the adaptation. Carbohydrate in the bottle rather than chewing your way there. Next weekend is the Alps and 5 September is the last specific day, so land Monday intact rather than fit.
